metadata.title: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition

summary.tldr: Pioneered gradient-based end-to-end backpropagation training for deep convolutional networks (LeNet-5), combining weight sharing, local receptive fields, and sub-sampling.
keyTakeaways: Introduced the classic Conv -> Pool -> Conv -> Pool -> FC pipeline for visual pattern recognition.
Demonstrated that weight sharing across spatial receptive fields drastically reduces parameters compared to fully connected layers.
Successfully deployed on commercial bank check digit recognition systems.

motivation.problemStatement: Traditional handwritten character recognition relied on handcrafted feature extractors combined with separate classifiers, failing to generalize to spatial shifts, scale variations, and geometric distortions.
previousLimitations: Fully connected networks suffered from parameter explosion when processing raw 2D pixel grids.
Handcrafted feature extractors lost spatial topology and were domain-specific.
Absence of end-to-end gradient optimization across feature extractors.
motivation.coreInsight: 2D image pixels have strong local spatial correlations. By constraining convolutional weights to be shared across spatially shifted receptive fields, feature maps acquire translation invariance while drastically reducing parameter count.
contributions: Formulated the LeNet-5 CNN architecture for 2D character recognition.
Introduced spatial sub-sampling (average pooling) to build translation tolerance.
Demonstrated backpropagation training end-to-end directly from raw pixel intensities.

innovations.title: Shared Weights & Local Receptive Fields
innovations.summary: Constrains 2D spatial filter weights to be reused across all pixel positions in a feature map.
innovations.detailedDescription: Instead of assigning independent weights to every pixel, a 5x5 kernel slides across the 32x32 input grid. All units in a feature map share the exact same weight vector and bias, enforcing translation invariance.

math.latexFormula: y_{i,j} = f\left( \sum_{m} \sum_{n} w_{m,n} \cdot x_{i+m, j+n} + b \right)
math.explanation: Standard 2D convolution equation with shared weight matrix w and activation f.

variables.description: Local 2D pixel intensity at spatial offset (m, n)
Shared kernel weight at spatial position (m, n)
Shared scalar bias term for feature map

math.significance: Reduces parameter footprint from O(N_input * N_output) to O(Kernel_size * Feature_maps).

ablationStudies.title: LeNet-5 vs Fully Connected Multi-Layer Perceptron
ablationStudies.description: Compared 5-layer CNN against a 3-layer fully connected MLP on raw 28x28 pixels.
ablationStudies.performanceDelta: Fully connected MLP suffered higher error rate (2.95%) and severe overfitting due to lack of spatial inductive bias.

evidence.reproducibilityNotes: Trained using stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with custom weight initialization and scaled hyperbolic tangent activation functions.

criticalNotes.title: Foundational CNN Blueprint
criticalNotes.content: Established the universal paradigm for all subsequent convolutional networks.

criticalNotes.title: Bounded by 1990s Compute Bounds
criticalNotes.content: Restricted to low-resolution grayscale images (32x32) due to CPU hardware limits of 1998.

lineage.title: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
lineage.description: Scaled LeNet's Conv-Pool-FC paradigm to high-resolution color images using GPU acceleration.

researchGaps: How to scale ConvNets to high-resolution RGB datasets without vanishing gradients?
How to accelerate backpropagation using GPU hardware parallelization?

reference.originalAbstract: Multilayer neural networks trained with backpropagation algorithms are best prepared for document recognition applications. We present LeNet-5, a convolutional neural network designed for handwritten character recognition.
